analysis:
Integration across all six unit analyses: the supplied PR content is documentation and test-only. The files are changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md, docs/architecture/inference.md, docs/developer/test.md, docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md, a new opt-in ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift, and a libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (14661d9 to 2068c93). No production Swift source diff was visible, so I could not evaluate the code behind the docs. No concrete regression is supported by the visible evidence, and I discard no candidate findings.

Coverage limits needing deeper review (T-041, T-028, TB-007, A-001): (1) The submodule bump hides the real change. The docs say provider-staged checkpoint destinations use zeroed host bytes, with no MLX evalLock and up to 64 MiB of transient host commit outside the MLX allocator. A reviewer must check the staging allocation bounds and the GlobalKVCacheBudget accounting. A reviewer must also check that staged destinations cannot be read before the authenticated AES-GCM payload fills them, so there is no cross-request KV leakage. The same pass must check that identity and cacheSalt binding is preserved and that there is no plaintext residue in host buffers. (2) The bounded fallback retry and read budgets are also unverified. (3) Doc claims that must remain consistent with T-041: 1800s TTL cap, HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 encryption, per-donation gating and CacheVolume checks. The base docs match T-041 and the visible head excerpts do not loosen them. (4) The new live test uses env -i, an isolated ephemeral cache and tenant-scoped foreign requests. It adds no production attack surface. It measures restore TTFT under contention, which is the already-accepted SEC-035 timing oracle and is unchanged in kind. Recommend a follow-up code-level review of the mlx-swift-lm diff and the provider files CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, CheckpointHostZeros.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift and CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift.
